         Pursuant to the widespread reports of excess admissions and deaths due to respiratory illness in China, possibly reported as part of the unknown pneumonia reporting system, enhanced surveillance is being planned.

nodes.author: agarwalamberr
nodes.text:
@AskSubramanian Sir
People using multiplex PCR can collate their data.

nodes.author: AskSubramanian
nodes.text: There are reports of a significant excess in admissions for respiratory infections. Although there has been no confirmation of this from either the Chinese authorities or the WHO, reports indicate that the numbers are significantly out of proportion to what is expected.

nodes.author: AskSubramanian
nodes.text: A spike in respiratory infections is anticipated in the colder months, and this seasonality is usual. The magnitude of the situation is what is being evaluated.

nodes.author: AskSubramanian
nodes.text: Preliminary data suggests that there are cases of infections due to multiple pathogens- influenza A, SARS-CoV2, Mycoplasma and the agent of concern, human meta pneumo virus (HMPV). The Chinese CDC data suggests that influenza A is the primary driver- 30.2% of the positive cases,

nodes.author: AskSubramanian
nodes.text:
but HMPV is linked to 6.2%- higher than adenovirus or SARS CoV2. 
HMPV is a respiratory RNA virus in the same family as RSV, and was discovered in 2001. It has been noted to cause a flu like illness in all age groups.

nodes.author: AskSubramanian
nodes.text: It is indistinguishable from other respiratory viruses by clinical presentation alone. In most healthy people, it tends to be mild self limiting illness. It can be severe in those with defective immune systems, and result in lung injury which requires ICU care.

nodes.author: AskSubramanian
nodes.text: At this point, there is no clear reason to expect another global pandemic, or a situation to stockpile resources. It is extremely likely that this is an extremely bad flu/cold season, and monitoring of the situation can clarify the issue.

nodes.author: AskSubramanian
nodes.text: Following the lessons learnt through the pandemic- distancing, making and hand hygiene should be adequate to ensure safety.
